entities.name: Neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Central nervous system infection caused by the larval metacestode stage (cysticerci) of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium, representing the leading identifiable cause of acquired adult-onset epilepsy in endemic regions worldwide.

entities.name: Adult-onset epilepsy
entities.description: Recurrent unprovoked epileptic seizures developing in adult life in an individual residing in or emigrating from a Taenia solium endemic region.

entities.name: Focal motor seizures
entities.description: Epileptic seizure activity characterized by unilateral motor jerking, twitching, or clonic movements reflecting localized cortical cyst involvement.

entities.name: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures
entities.description: Bilateral convulsive seizures involving loss of consciousness, tonic contraction, and rhythmic clonic jerking throughout all extremities.

entities.name: Focal sensory seizures
entities.description: Epileptic paroxysms presenting with unilateral paresthesias, numbness, or tingling sensations corresponding to primary somatosensory cortex.

entities.name: Impaired awareness seizures
entities.description: Focal seizures associated with clouded consciousness, behavioral arrest, or motor automatisms, commonly originating from temporal lobe structures.

entities.name: Status epilepticus
entities.description: Continuous or rapidly repeating seizures lasting over 5 minutes without recovery of consciousness, representing a neurological emergency.

entities.name: Chronic throbbing headache
entities.description: Persistent severe tension-type, hemicranial, or pulsating headaches present in over one-third of neurocysticercosis patients.

entities.name: Intracranial hypertension
entities.description: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid pressure manifesting with severe holocranial headache, projectile vomiting, and visual obscurations.

entities.name: Parenchymal neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Localization of Taenia solium metacestode larvae within the brain cortex and subcortical white matter, representing 60% to 80% of infections.

entities.name: Extraparenchymal neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Involvement of ventricular spaces, subarachnoid cisterns, spine, or eyes, characterized by aggressive course and elevated morbidity.

entities.name: Intraventricular neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Parasitic cyst formation within cerebral ventricles, predominantly the fourth ventricle, causing mechanical CSF obstruction.

entities.name: Subarachnoid neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Colonization of cerebral fissures and basal cisterns by cysticerci, triggering intense proliferative fibrotic leptomeningitis.

entities.name: Racemose neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Atypical proliferating metacestode form lacking a scolex that grows by continuous budding into giant multiloculated cisternal cyst clusters.

entities.name: Cysticercotic meningitis
entities.description: Chronic basilar leptomeningitis elicited by degenerating subarachnoid cysticerci releasing foreign cestode antigens into the CSF.

entities.name: Obstructive hydrocephalus
entities.description: Dilation of cerebral ventricles upstream of a physical barrier to CSF flow caused by an intraventricular cyst or granular ependymitis.

entities.name: Communicating hydrocephalus
entities.description: Impaired resorption of CSF at arachnoid granulations caused by chronic inflammatory exudate and fibrosis in the basal cisterns.

entities.name: Ischemic stroke
entities.description: Acute focal neurological deficit caused by inflammatory arterial occlusion in patients with basal cisternal neurocysticercosis.

entities.name: Transient ischemic attack
entities.description: Reversible episode of neurological dysfunction caused by transient focal cerebral ischemia in the territory of inflamed basal vessels.

entities.name: Cranial nerve palsies
entities.description: Focal deficits of cranial nerves arising from direct compression or inflammatory entrapment by basilar subarachnoid cysticerci.

entities.name: Cognitive impairment
entities.description: Subacute or chronic decline in memory, executive function, and attention provoked by multiple parenchymal cysts or chronic hydrocephalus.

entities.name: Psychiatric symptoms
entities.description: Affective and behavioral disturbances including major depression, psychosis, confusion, and psychomotor agitation.

entities.name: Cysticercal encephalitis
entities.description: Hyperacute life-threatening diffuse encephalopathy caused by a massive immune reaction against dozens to hundreds of degenerating parenchymal cysts.

entities.name: Visual acuity loss
entities.description: Progressive or abrupt impairment of vision caused by chronic papilledema, optochiasmatic arachnoiditis, or intraocular cysts.

entities.name: Visual field defects
entities.description: Loss of visual field sectors such as bitemporal hemianopia or quadrantanopia from optochiasmatic cyst compression.

entities.name: Intraocular cysticercosis
entities.description: Localization of the larval metacestode within the vitreous chamber or subretinal space of the eyeball.

entities.name: Spinal neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Metacestode infection involving the spinal cord parenchyma or spinal subarachnoid leptomeninges.

entities.name: Spinal cord compression
entities.description: Myelopathic syndrome of progressive motor paralysis, sensory deficit, and hyperreflexia caused by an expanding intramedullary or extramedullary cyst.

entities.name: Radicular neuropathic pain
entities.description: Sharp shooting dermatomal nerve pain resulting from chemical or mechanical irritation of spinal dorsal nerve roots by cysts.

entities.name: Ataxic gait
entities.description: Broad-based, uncoordinated walking pattern reflecting cerebellar hemisphere involvement, vermian compression, or sensory ataxia.

entities.name: Vertiginous dizziness
entities.description: True spinning vertigo or severe dizziness provoked by vestibular nuclear or cerebellar pathway compromise.

entities.name: Projectile vomiting
entities.description: Forceful expulsion of gastric contents without preceding nausea, characteristic of sudden intracranial pressure spikes.

entities.name: Altered mental status
entities.description: Fluctuating level of consciousness ranging from somnolence and confusion to stupor and unresponsiveness.

entities.name: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction
entities.description: Endocrine derangement including hypopituitarism, hyperprolactinemia, or diabetes insipidus caused by parasellar cysts.

entities.name: Subcutaneous cysticercosis
entities.description: Presence of painless, firm, mobile cysts within subcutaneous and adipose tissues, coexisting with CNS infection.

entities.name: Muscular pseudohypertrophy
entities.description: Generalized enlargement of skeletal muscle bellies caused by heavy infiltration of viable and calcifying metacestode cysts.

entities.name: Progressive hemiparesis
entities.description: Unilateral motor weakness of face, arm, and leg progressing over days to weeks due to mass effect or arterial vasculopathy.

entities.name: Dysphasia
entities.description: Impaired expressive or receptive speech output resulting from dominant perisylvian cerebral cortical cyst localization.

entities.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
entities.description: Subarachnoid or intraparenchymal bleeding provoked by cysticercal mycotic pseudoaneurysm rupture or hemorrhagic venous infarction.

entities.name: Parinaud syndrome
entities.description: Dorsal midbrain syndrome characterized by upward gaze palsy, convergence-retraction nystagmus, and light-near pupillary dissociation.

entities.name: Sleep disturbances
entities.description: Disrupted circadian sleep architecture, insomnia, or hypersomnolence resulting from central neuroinflammatory cytokine signaling.

entities.name: Bruns syndrome
entities.description: Paroxysmal attacks of severe positional occipital headache, vertigo, vomiting, and syncope triggered by sudden head rotation.

entities.name: Subcutaneous cystic nodules
entities.description: Palpable, painless, mobile, rubbery flesh-colored subcutaneous nodules containing intact or degenerating Taenia solium cysticerci.

entities.name: Subretinal larval cyst
entities.description: Direct funduscopic visualization of a well-defined translucent retinal cysticercus with undulating movement and visible invaginated scolex.

entities.name: Papilledema
entities.description: Bilateral swelling of optic nerve head with blurred disc margins, hyperemia, and loss of venous pulsations reflecting elevated ICP.

entities.name: Todd paralysis
entities.description: Transient focal motor weakness or flaccid hemiparesis following a focal epileptic seizure, persisting from minutes to 48 hours.

entities.name: Nuchal rigidity
entities.description: Resistance to passive neck flexion caused by reflex spasm of extensor muscles from chronic meningeal irritation.

entities.name: Positive Kernig sign
entities.description: Inability to extend the knee beyond 135 degrees when the hip is flexed at 90 degrees due to painful hamstring spasm.

entities.name: Positive Brudzinski sign
entities.description: Involuntary flexion of the hips and knees upon passive flexion of the patient's neck, indicating meningeal irritation.

entities.name: Sixth nerve palsy
entities.description: Failure of eye abduction with horizontal diplopia on lateral gaze resulting from abducens nerve traction or inflammation.

entities.name: Third nerve palsy
entities.description: Ptosis, pupillary dilation, and unreactive down-and-out ocular deviation caused by oculomotor nerve compression.

entities.name: Seventh nerve palsy
entities.description: Unilateral facial droop with impaired forehead wrinkling and incomplete eye closure characteristic of lower motor neuron facial paresis.

entities.name: Optic disc atrophy
entities.description: Pale, chalky optic nerve head with vessel attenuation indicating permanent axonal loss from chronic papilledema.

entities.name: Hyperreflexia
entities.description: Abnormally brisk, exaggerated deep tendon reflexes denoting corticospinal pyramidal tract disinhibition.

entities.name: Positive Babinski sign
entities.description: Dorsiflexion of the great toe with fanning of other toes on plantar stroking indicating upper motor neuron lesion.

entities.name: Pronator drift
entities.description: Downward drifting and pronation of an outstretched, supinated arm with eyes closed indicating subtle upper motor neuron weakness.

entities.name: Dysmetria
entities.description: Inability to properly judge distance or scale during coordinated movement, evidenced by past-pointing on finger-to-nose testing.

entities.name: Dysdiadochokinesia
entities.description: Inability to perform rapid, alternating movements such as forearm pronation-supination smoothly and rhythmically.

entities.name: Truncal ataxia
entities.description: Inability to maintain steady upright posture while sitting or standing without lateral or anteroposterior swaying.

entities.name: Spastic paraparesis
entities.description: Bilateral lower extremity weakness accompanied by increased muscle tone, hyperreflexia, and clasp-knife rigidity.

entities.name: Sensory level deficit
entities.description: Sharp horizontal demarcation on the trunk below which pinprick, temperature, or light touch sensations are diminished.

entities.name: Ankle clonus
entities.description: Series of rhythmic, involuntary muscular contractions and relaxations elicited by sudden passive dorsiflexion of the ankle.

entities.name: Homonymous hemianopia
entities.description: Visual field loss in the same half of the visual field in both eyes resulting from post-chiasmatic optic tract or radiation lesion.

entities.name: Marcus Gunn pupil
entities.description: Paradoxical pupillary dilation when light is swung from the unaffected to the affected eye during swinging-flashlight test.

entities.name: Cushing triad
entities.description: Life-threatening clinical triad of severe bradycardia, irregular respirations, and widening pulse pressure with systolic hypertension.

entities.name: Decerebrate posturing
entities.description: Abnormal body posture involving rigid extension of the arms and legs, downward pointing of toes, and backward arching of the head.

entities.name: Decorticate posturing
entities.description: Abnormal posture involving adduction and flexion of arms at the elbows with clenched fists and extended lower extremities.

entities.name: Glabellar tap sign
entities.description: Failure to habituate to repetitive tapping on the forehead between the eyebrows, with persistent blinking (Myerson sign).

entities.name: Hypalgesia
entities.description: Decreased sensitivity to painful stimuli such as pinprick in a focal, dermatomal, or hemi-distribution.

entities.name: Hole-with-dot imaging sign
entities.description: Pathognomonic neuroimaging finding: rounded cystic cavity containing an eccentric punctate mural nodule representing the invaginated scolex.

entities.name: Vesicular stage cyst
entities.description: Viable translucent cyst containing clear fluid and an intact scolex, showing thin non-enhancing walls and no surrounding edema.

entities.name: Colloidal vesicular cyst
entities.description: Degenerating cysticercus with turbid fluid, thick ring-enhancing capsule, and prominent surrounding vasogenic edema.

entities.name: Granular nodular lesion
entities.description: Involuting stage characterized by cyst collapse, thick fibrotic capsule, nodular rim enhancement, and diminishing edema.

entities.name: Calcified nodular scar
entities.description: Non-viable, densely mineralized, inactive 2 to 5 mm round hyperdense punctate nodule on non-contrast CT without active edema.

entities.name: Perilesional vasogenic edema
entities.description: High T2/FLAIR signal in cerebral white matter radiating outward from an inflamed colloidal or granular cysticercal lesion.

entities.name: Enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot
entities.description: Serum Western blot using lentil lectin-purified Taenia solium glycoprotein antigens (LL-GP), the serological gold standard.

entities.name: Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis
entities.description: Elevated WBC count in CSF (10 to 300 cells/uL) predominantly comprised of lymphocytes and mononuclear cells in meningeal disease.

entities.name: Elevated CSF protein
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid protein concentration ranging between 50 and 300 mg/dL denoting blood-CSF barrier breakdown.

entities.name: Normal CSF glucose
entities.description: Preserved CSF glucose concentration (>40 mg/dL or CSF:serum ratio >0.5) typical of non-bacterial neurohelminthic infection.

entities.name: CSF eosinophilia
entities.description: Presence of eosinophils accounting for >5% of CSF leukocytes, strongly indicating neuroparasitic or helminthic infection.

entities.name: Normal peripheral leukocytes
entities.description: Complete blood count showing total white blood cell count within reference limits (4,000 to 10,000 cells/uL) without bandemia.

entities.name: Mild peripheral eosinophilia
entities.description: Peripheral blood eosinophil proportion of 5% to 10% (absolute eosinophil count 500 to 1,500 cells/uL) present in a minority of cases.

entities.name: Elevated opening pressure
entities.description: Lumbar puncture manometry opening pressure exceeding 200 to 250 mm H2O in lateral decubitus position.

entities.name: FIESTA sequence MRI
entities.description: Fast Imaging Employing Steady-state Acquisition MRI optimizing contrast between CSF and non-enhancing thin cyst membranes.

entities.name: CISS sequence MRI
entities.description: Constructive Interference in Steady State MRI sequence providing high-resolution submillimeter imaging of CSF cisterns.

entities.name: Basilar arachnoidal thickening
entities.description: Abnormal diffuse contrast enhancement and fibrotic thickening along the leptomeninges of the prepontine, interpeduncular, and chiasmatic cisterns.

entities.name: Racemose cyst clusters
entities.description: Multiloculated, grape-like cisternal cystic masses with thin septations lacking visible scolices on high-resolution MRI.

entities.name: Ventricular outflow obstruction
entities.description: Disproportionate ventricular dilation proximal to an intraventricular cystic mass causing acute non-communicating hydrocephalus.

entities.name: Fourth ventricle dilation
entities.description: Selective ballooning and expansion of the fourth ventricle cavity harboring an encysted or free-floating larval metacestode.

entities.name: Aqueductal stenosis
entities.description: Narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius with upstream lateral and third ventriculomegaly caused by granular ependymitis.

entities.name: Periventricular transependymal edema
entities.description: Hyperintense T2/FLAIR periventricular halos around lateral ventricular frontal horns indicating acute hydrocephalic CSF transudation.

entities.name: Non-contrast brain CT
entities.description: Primary emergency triage neuroimaging modality with high sensitivity for detecting hyperdense calcified granulomas.

entities.name: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI
entities.description: Definitive imaging modality for characterizing cysticercal viability, scolex anatomy, and inflammatory capsules.

entities.name: DWI non-restriction
entities.description: Absence of bright hyperintense signal on diffusion-weighted imaging with preserved high ADC, indicating non-viscous cyst fluid.

entities.name: Elevated choline-creatine ratio
entities.description: MR spectroscopy metabolite alteration demonstrating elevated choline, acetate, and succinate with decreased N-acetylaspartate.

entities.name: Parasitic lactate peak
entities.description: Proton MR spectroscopy resonance peak at 1.3 ppm representing parasitic anaerobic glycolysis metabolites including lactate and succinate.

entities.name: Cerebral angiography arteritis
entities.description: Catheter or CT angiography demonstrating focal lumen narrowing, beading, and ectasia of basal cerebral arteries.

entities.name: EEG focal slowing
entities.description: Electroencephalographic polymorphic delta or theta wave slowing over the cortical region overlying an inflamed cyst.

entities.name: Spike-wave epileptiform discharges
entities.description: Focal sharp waves, spike-wave complexes, or paroxysmal epileptiform discharges corresponding to epileptogenic perilesional gliosis.

entities.name: Serum cysticercal antigen
entities.description: Detection of circulating excretory-secretory metacestode glycoprotein antigens (HP10/B158 mAb) in serum or CSF.

entities.name: Stool microscopy examination
entities.description: Microscopic identification of Taenia eggs or gravid proglottids in fecal wet mounts or Kato-Katz thick smears.

entities.name: Soft tissue calcifications
entities.description: Characteristic elongated 'cigar-shaped' or oval calcified nodules aligned along muscle fiber axes on plain soft-tissue radiographs.

entities.name: Ocular B-scan ultrasonography
entities.description: Ophthalmic ultrasound demonstrating a well-defined anechoic cystic cavity with a highly reflective eccentric mural scolex.

entities.name: Subcutaneous nodule ultrasound
entities.description: High-frequency soft-tissue ultrasound revealing a well-defined oval cystic mass containing an eccentric hyperechoic nidus.

entities.name: Normal erythrocyte sedimentation
entities.description: Baseline erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) within normal clinical limits (<20 mm/hr).

entities.name: Normal C-reactive protein
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein level within reference range (<5 to 10 mg/L) at admission triage.

entities.name: Spinal intradural cyst
entities.description: Well-demarcated intradural extramedullary cystic mass on spinal MRI causing local cord or cauda equina compression.

entities.name: Taenia solium eggs
entities.description: Infective microscopic oncosphere-containing eggs passed in the stool of an infected human tapeworm carrier.

entities.name: Tapeworm household contact
entities.description: Cohabitation with an individual harboring an adult intestinal Taenia solium tapeworm shedding infective eggs.

entities.name: Contaminated drinking water
entities.description: Unfiltered or untreated domestic water supplies contaminated by human fecal runoff containing viable tapeworm eggs.

entities.name: Contaminated raw produce
entities.description: Raw agricultural vegetables and fruits fertilized with human night soil or irrigated with sewage water.

entities.name: Free-roaming domestic swine
entities.description: Domestic pig husbandry where swine have unrestricted access to open human defecation areas and sewage.

entities.name: Lack of latrines
entities.description: Absence of sanitary enclosed toilet facilities resulting in widespread open human defecation near living and grazing areas.

entities.name: Unregulated home slaughter
entities.description: Clandestine backyard butchering of domestic pigs without official veterinary inspection for 'measly pork' cysticerci.

entities.name: Endemic rural communities
entities.description: Agrarian settlements in developing countries where poverty, substandard sanitation, and pig farming intersect.

entities.name: Subsistence pig farmers
entities.description: Smallholder agricultural families who raise backyard pigs under primitive sanitary conditions without veterinary oversight.

entities.name: Household food preparers
entities.description: Domestic or commercial food handlers harboring tapeworms who contaminate meals through inadequate hand hygiene.

entities.name: Rural agricultural workers
entities.description: Farm laborers who work in fields exposed to sewage irrigation or lack access to handwashing facilities.

entities.name: International endemic travelers
entities.description: Tourists, expatriates, and travelers visiting friends and relatives in hyperendemic developing regions.

entities.name: Household taeniasis carrier
entities.description: Index patient carrying adult Taenia solium tapeworm in the gut, acting as the contagious focus for whole households.

entities.name: Close contact clusters
entities.description: Family or institutional groups sharing living spaces, toilets, or food with an active tapeworm carrier.

entities.name: Prolonged clinical latency
entities.description: Prolonged asymptomatic incubation period of 2 to 5 years, and up to decades, between egg ingestion and symptom onset.

entities.name: Multi-year incubation period
entities.description: Extended period during which viable metacestodes evade host immunity and persist in CNS parenchyma without symptoms.

entities.name: Variable incubation interval
entities.description: Widely variable onset timeframe governed by cyst location, larval burden, and the timing of host immune recognition.

entities.name: Fecal-oral autoinfection
entities.description: Direct self-inoculation of eggs by a tapeworm carrier via contaminated fingers or reverse gastric peristalsis.

entities.name: Endemic Latin America
entities.description: High-prevalence geographic zone across rural Mexico, Central America, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, and Brazil.

entities.name: Endemic South Asia
entities.description: High-burden region encompassing northern, southern, and eastern states of India, Nepal, and Bhutan.

entities.name: Endemic sub-Saharan Africa
entities.description: Expanding hyperendemic zone throughout eastern, central, and southern agrarian regions of Africa.

entities.name: Endemic Southeast Asia
entities.description: Focal endemic foci in agrarian areas of Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, and non-Islamic Indonesian islands (Bali).

entities.name: Pork ingestion alone
entities.description: Consumption of infected pork meat without fecal egg ingestion, which produces only intestinal taeniasis.

entities.name: Acute purulent CSF
entities.description: Grossly turbid or purulent cerebrospinal fluid with thousands of polymorphonuclear neutrophils.

entities.name: Spiking high fever
entities.description: Acute high spiking fever (>39 deg C) accompanied by toxic rigors and septic delirium.

entities.name: Marked peripheral leukocytosis
entities.description: Significant leukocytosis (>15,000 WBC/uL) with pronounced left shift and bandemia on admission CBC.

entities.name: Restricted cyst DWI
entities.description: Central hyperintense diffusion restriction on DWI with low ADC mapping within a cystic mass.

entities.name: Internal daughter cysts
entities.description: Massive cystic brain mass containing multiple internal daughter vesicles, septa, or hydatid sand.

entities.name: Floating hydatid membrane
entities.description: Detached, undulating parasite endocyst membrane floating within cyst cavity ('water-lily sign').

entities.name: Shaggy infiltrative mass
entities.description: Thick, grossly irregular, nodular, shaggy enhancing mass with central necrosis and infiltrative brain margins.

entities.name: Severe midline shift
entities.description: Rapid massive brain displacement with midline shift exceeding 10 to 15 mm caused by invasive tumor bulk.

entities.name: Extensive calvarial erosion
entities.description: Direct osteolytic destruction of the cranial vault with transcalvarial invasion into scalp soft tissues.

entities.name: Negative neuroimaging study
entities.description: Completely normal high-resolution contrast-enhanced brain CT and MRI without cysts, scars, or edema.

entities.name: Hypoglycorrhachia below twenty
entities.description: Profound depression of CSF glucose concentration (<20 mg/dL or CSF-to-serum glucose ratio <0.2).

entities.name: Acid-fast bacilli smear
entities.description: Microscopic demonstration of red acid-fast rods on Ziehl-Neelsen or auramine-rhodamine CSF staining.

entities.name: Serum cryptococcal antigen
entities.description: Positive lateral flow immunoassay for Cryptococcus capsular glucuronoxylomannan antigen in serum or CSF.

entities.name: Positive CSF gram
entities.description: Direct microscopic visualization of Gram-positive or Gram-negative bacteria on CSF smear.

entities.name: Choroid plexus papilloma
entities.description: Lobulated, cauliflower-like, vividly vascular intraventricular neoplasm arising from choroid plexus.

entities.name: Multiple punctate microbleeds
entities.description: Diffuse petechial cerebral microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) or GRE sequences.

entities.name: Hyperacute stroke syndrome
entities.description: Maximal sudden focal deficit onset within seconds to minutes in an elderly vasculopathic patient without preceding seizures.

entities.name: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
entities.description: Extensive, diffuse, sheet-like nodular malignant seeding coating the entire spinal cord and brainstem.

entities.name: Pure beef exposure
entities.description: Dietary exposure limited strictly to undercooked beef containing Taenia saginata cysticerci.

entities.name: Marked procalcitonin elevation
entities.description: Serum procalcitonin exceeding 2.0 ng/mL indicating severe invasive systemic bacterial sepsis.

entities.name: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
entities.description: Septic thrombosis of cavernous sinus manifesting with chemosis, proptosis, and bilateral ophthalmoplegia.

entities.name: Cerebral tuberculoma
entities.description: Intracranial granuloma caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis presenting as ring-enhancing mass lesions.

entities.name: Pyogenic brain abscess
entities.description: Focal intracranial bacterial infection with central pus collection presenting as ring-enhancing lesion.

entities.name: Cerebral echinococcosis
entities.description: Hydatid cyst infection of brain caused by larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus or multilocularis.

entities.name: High-grade glioma
entities.description: Malignant primary brain tumor (glioblastoma) presenting as an invasive ring-enhancing cerebral mass in adults.

entities.name: Brain metastases
entities.description: Secondary malignant intracranial neoplasms presenting with ring enhancement at corticomedullary junctions.

entities.name: Cerebral toxoplasmosis
entities.description: Opportunistic protozoan infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii producing ring-enhancing lesions in immunocompromised hosts.

entities.name: Tuberculous meningitis
entities.description: Subacute granulomatous leptomeningitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis with thick basilar exudates.

entities.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
entities.description: Opportunistic fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus neoformans causing chronic meningitis in immunocompromised patients.

entities.name: Primary CNS lymphoma
entities.description: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma restricted to central nervous system presenting with periventricular enhancing lesions.

entities.name: Arachnoid cyst
entities.description: Congenital extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid collection contained within split layers of arachnoid membrane.

entities.name: Epidermoid cyst
entities.description: Congenital intracranial inclusion cyst lined by squamous epithelium filled with cholesterol and desquamated keratin.

entities.name: Neurovascular stroke
entities.description: Atherothrombotic or cardioembolic acute cerebral infarction presenting with focal neurological deficits.

entities.name: Viral encephalitis
entities.description: Acute viral brain parenchymal infection commonly caused by Herpes simplex virus presenting with fever and confusion.

entities.name: Intracranial hydatid cyst
entities.description: Expansive parasitic cyst caused by Echinococcus granulosus developing within the cerebral hemispheres.

entities.name: Bacterial meningitis
entities.description: Acute purulent infection of the subarachnoid space caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, or Listeria.

entities.name: Multiple sclerosis
entities.description: Autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by relapsing-remitting neurological episodes and dissemination in space and time.

entities.name: Cavernous malformation
entities.description: Vascular hamartoma of the CNS composed of endothelial-lined sinusoidal spaces containing slow-moving blood.

entities.name: Colloid cyst
entities.description: Benign congenital mucin-containing cyst located in anterior third ventricle that can cause acute hydrocephalus.

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with adult-onset epilepsy in 70% to 90% of symptomatic parenchymal cases, resulting from epileptogenic gliotic scars around calcified cysts or active inflammatory host responses to degenerating larvae.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as focal motor seizures with or without secondary generalization, frequently originating from cortical or subcortical convexity cysts irritative to adjacent motor cortex.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as generalized tonic-clonic convulsions, commonly evolving from secondary generalization of focal epileptogenic discharges provoked by degenerating colloidal cysticerci.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as focal sensory seizures when cysticerci lodge in or adjacent to the postcentral gyrus or parietal somatosensory cortices.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as focal impaired awareness seizures with behavioral arrest or automatisms when cysticerci involve the mesial temporal lobe or amygdalohippocampal complex.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as refractory convulsive status epilepticus provoked by acute massive perilesional inflammatory edema or rapid simultaneous breakdown of multiple colloidal cysts.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as chronic throbbing headaches in 35% to 50% of symptomatic patients, provoked by local dural irritation, perilesional inflammation, or intermittent increases in intracranial pressure.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intracranial hypertension resulting from non-communicating ventricular blockage, extensive communicating hydrocephalus from basal arachnoiditis, or diffuse brain edema.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as parenchymal neurocysticercosis in 60% to 80% of clinical cases, progressing sequentially through vesicular, colloidal, granular, and calcified stages.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as extraparenchymal neurocysticercosis with high risk of hydrocephalus, progressive intracranial hypertension, chronic meningitis, and cerebrovascular infarction.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intraventricular neurocysticercosis in 10% to 20% of patients, frequently lodging within the fourth ventricle and precipitating acute non-communicating hydrocephalus.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as subarachnoid neurocysticercosis within the Sylvian fissures and basilar cisterns, provoking marked inflammatory arachnoiditis and multiple cranial neuropathies.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as racemose neurocysticercosis characterized by giant, grape-like budding cystic clusters within basal cisterns that expand without forming scolices and compress vital brainstem structures.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as cysticercotic meningitis with chronic lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis, high protein, and basilar fibrotic thickening, mimicking chronic tuberculous or fungal meningitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute or subacute obstructive hydrocephalus when cysts lodge in the foramen of Monro, cerebral aqueduct, or fourth ventricle exit foramina.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as communicating hydrocephalus secondary to severe basilar arachnoiditis obstructing CSF pathway transit through the tentorial incisura to cortical convexity arachnoid granulations.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as ischemic cerebrovascular stroke in 2% to 12% of patients due to endarteritis obliterans of major cerebral vessels traversing inflamed subarachnoid cisterns.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as transient ischemic attacks precipitated by fluctuating inflammatory cerebral vasculopathy and transient hypoperfusion around basal cisternal cysts.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as multiple cranial nerve palsies, most commonly affecting cranial nerves II, III, VI, and VII, as they traverse thickened basal cisternal exudate.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as progressive cognitive impairment or dementia in 5% to 15% of patients with extensive parenchymal cyst burden, chronic hydrocephalus, or repeated cerebral infarcts.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as psychiatric disturbances including major depressive disorder, apathy, and psychosis, particularly in long-standing disease with limbic or frontal lobe cysts.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as cysticercal encephalitis primarily in children and young women with massive cyst loads who present with severe diffuse cerebral edema, coma, and intractable seizures.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as progressive visual acuity loss and eventual blindness secondary to prolonged untreated intracranial hypertension, optic atrophy, or direct intraocular parasitic invasion.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as visual field deficits when subarachnoid cysts in the suprasellar cistern compress the optic chiasm or retrochiasmatic optic radiations.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intraocular cysticercosis in 1% to 3% of cases, featuring visible subretinal or intravitreal parasites causing vitritis, retinal detachment, and leukocoria.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as spinal neurocysticercosis in 1% to 5% of cases, producing progressive lower extremity weakness, sensory levels, and sphincter incontinence from cord compression.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute or subacute spinal cord compression when cysticerci migrate into the spinal subarachnoid space or develop within the spinal cord parenchyma.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe radicular neuropathic pain in lumbar or thoracic nerve distributions secondary to leptomeningeal cyst inflammation and cauda equina irritation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as an unsteady, ataxic gait resulting from cerebellar parenchymal cysts, fourth ventricle cystic distention, or obstructive hydrocephalus with truncal ataxia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intense vertiginous dizziness and dysequilibrium from fourth ventricular cysticerci abutting vestibular nuclei in the floor of the fourth ventricle.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as paroxysmal projectile vomiting without gastrointestinal prodrome, triggered by sudden acute elevations in intracranial pressure or stimulation of the area postrema.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as altered mental status, drowsiness, and progressive lethargy during acute hydrocephalic decompensation or extensive colloidal stage neuroinflammation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as hypothalamic-pituitary neuroendocrine dysfunction when subarachnoid cysts expand into the sellar and suprasellar regions, compressing the pituitary stalk.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as painless subcutaneous cystic nodules (more frequent in Asian patients) that provide an accessible bedside clinical clue to underlying neurocysticercosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as muscular pseudohypertrophy and weakness in rare disseminated cysticercosis cases where hundreds of larvae populate skeletal muscles.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as progressive contralateral hemiparesis from expanding colloidal cysts in the motor cortex or internal capsule, or from cerebral arteritis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as motor expressive or sensory receptive dysphasia when colloidal cysts and surrounding vasogenic edema involve Broca or Wernicke dominant areas.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as atypical non-aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage or intracerebral hematoma caused by inflammatory erosion of vessel walls traversing basilar cisternal cysts.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as Parinaud dorsal midbrain syndrome when cysticerci in the quadrigeminal cistern or pineal region compress the superior colliculi and pretectal area.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as fragmented sleep patterns, daytime hypersomnolence, and insomnia secondary to chronic nocturnal intracranial hypertension and persistent headache.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, pathognomonic hallmark, physical exam sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Produces the pathognomonic Bruns syndrome: paroxysmal attacks of severe positional headache, vertigo, and syncope triggered by head rotation as a mobile 4th ventricular cyst causes ball-valve obstruction of CSF outflow.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, pathognomonic hallmark, physical exam sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features palpable, painless subcutaneous cystic nodules in skin and skeletal muscle that serve as a smoking-gun physical exam hallmark for systemic and central nervous system cysticercosis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, pathognomonic hallmark, physical exam sign
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Demonstrates direct funduscopic visualization of an undulating subretinal larval cyst with a visible white scolex, constituting Del Brutto's absolute pathognomonic criterion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates bilateral papilledema on funduscopic exam in patients presenting with intracranial hypertension secondary to hydrocephalus or extensive basilar arachnoiditis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits postictal Todd paralysis, where transient focal weakness in a limb confirms localized cortical motor seizure activity provoked by an adjacent colloidal cyst.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits palpable nuchal rigidity during neck flexion testing in patients with chronic cysticercotic basilar meningitis or subarachnoid cyst rupture.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits a positive Kernig sign on physical examination reflecting chronic inflammatory meningeal irritation in basal subarachnoid neurocysticercosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Displays a positive Brudzinski sign during bedside examination, confirming active meningeal inflammation provoked by subarachnoid metacestode breakdown.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals unilateral or bilateral sixth cranial nerve palsy as a false-localizing physical sign of raised intracranial pressure or direct basilar cisternal entrapment.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates complete or partial third cranial nerve palsy with ptosis and anisocoria due to cisternal cyst expansion in the interpeduncular fossa or impending uncal herniation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits peripheral seventh cranial nerve palsy from inflammatory entrapment within the cerebellopontine angle or internal auditory canal by basilar cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals chalky white secondary optic disc atrophy on direct ophthalmoscopy following chronic, unresolved papilledema or optochiasmatic arachnoiditis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Displays pathological hyperreflexia on deep tendon reflex testing in limbs contralateral to cortical parenchymal cysts or bilateral in spinal cord compression.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits an extensor plantar response (positive Babinski sign) indicating upper motor neuron corticospinal tract compromise from cortical, subcortical, or spinal cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates unilateral pronator drift of the upper extremity on bedside motor screening, detecting subtle corticospinal deficits from contralateral frontal cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits dysmetria on finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing when cerebellar hemisphere cysts or vermian lesions impair motor coordination.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals marked dysdiadochokinesia during rapid alternating movements, indicating cerebellar pathway involvement by cerebellar or intraventricular cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Displays truncal ataxia with broad-based stance and titubation due to fourth ventricular cysticercal mass effect or midline vermis compression.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Manifests as spastic paraparesis on lower extremity motor testing in patients with spinal intramedullary or extramedullary cysticerci compressing the thoracic spinal cord.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates a distinct sensory level on trunk pinprick examination, precisely localizing spinal cord compression by intradural cysticercal lesions.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits sustained ankle clonus (>5 beats) on rapid foot dorsiflexion, denoting severe upper motor neuron disinhibition from pyramidal tract lesion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Detects contralateral homonymous hemianopia on confrontation visual field testing in patients with occipital parenchymal cysts or optic radiation compression.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Displays a relative afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil) on swinging flashlight examination indicating asymmetric optic nerve injury from arachnoiditis or direct cyst compression.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exhibits the ominous Cushing triad (systolic hypertension with widened pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations) signalling imminent brain herniation from acute obstructive hydrocephalus.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates decerebrate extensor posturing on noxious stimulation in comatose patients suffering midbrain/upper pontine compression from severe uncal or central herniation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates decorticate flexor posturing indicating severe bilateral corticospinal damage at the diencephalic level in massive cysticercal encephalitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits persistent uninhibited blinking to glabellar tapping (Myerson sign) reflecting frontal lobe release from anterior frontal parenchymal cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam anchor, neurological sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates focal hypalgesia on pinprick sensation testing corresponding to cortical or thalamic sensory pathway disruption by inflammatory cysticerci.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Displays the pathognomonic 'hole-with-a-dot' neuroimaging sign on brain CT or MRI, where a cystic cavity contains an eccentric hyperdense or hyperintense mural nodule representing the invaginated scolex.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Appears on MRI/CT as a vesicular stage cyst: thin-walled, well-circumscribed, CSF-isointense lesion with an intact scolex without capsular enhancement or perilesional edema due to immune evasion.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Appears as a colloidal vesicular cyst on contrast CT/MRI with thick, regular ring-enhancement and extensive surrounding vasogenic edema reflecting intense host cell-mediated immune attack against degenerating larvae.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates a granular nodular lesion on contrast MRI/CT: a shrunken, involuting, nodular-enhancing granuloma with regressing perilesional vasogenic edema.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Visualizes on non-contrast brain CT as calcified nodular scars: discrete, hyperdense 2-5 mm non-enhancing mineralized foci devoid of active edema, representing non-viable chronic parasitic remnants.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Exhibits prominent finger-like perilesional vasogenic edema on T2/FLAIR MRI surrounding colloidal cysts, which serves as the primary driver of acute symptomatic seizures and headaches.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates serum enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot (EITB) seropositivity with >98% sensitivity and 100% specificity for patients with two or more viable parenchymal or extraparenchymal cysts.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows mild to moderate cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis (10-300 WBC/uL with mononuclear/lymphocytic predominance) in patients with subarachnoid or intraventricular neurocysticercosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits elevated CSF protein (50-300 mg/dL) at diagnostic lumbar puncture, reflecting chronic meningeal inflammation and blood-brain barrier permeability in basilar subarachnoid disease.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Displays normal or only mildly depressed CSF glucose levels, an important admission triage feature separating cysticercotic meningitis from bacterial or fungal meningitis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates CSF eosinophilia (eosinophils comprising 5% to 30% of CSF white cells), providing a valuable bedside lab clue for CNS helminthic infection when present.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits normal peripheral leukocyte counts on admission triage CBC without toxic granulation or significant bandemia, differentiating parenchymal NCC from bacterial pyogenic infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits mild peripheral blood eosinophilia (5-10%) in only 15% to 30% of cases; its absence does not rule out active neurocysticercosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates elevated opening pressure (>200-250 mm H2O) on lumbar puncture manometry in patients with subarachnoid cysts or communicating hydrocephalus.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Employs 3D FIESTA MRI sequences to provide exquisite contrast between cerebrospinal fluid and thin cyst membranes, clearly visualizing intraventricular and cisternal scolices missed on conventional T1/T2.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Utilizes 3D CISS MRI sequences to delineate subtle non-enhancing translucent metacestode cyst walls and floating scolices within the fourth ventricle and basilar cisterns.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals intense basilar arachnoidal thickening and leptomeningeal enhancement on post-gadolinium T1 MRI, indicating severe chronic inflammatory reaction to subarachnoid cysticerci.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Displays racemose cyst clusters on brain MRI: large, multi-lobulated, non-enhancing grape-like cystic structures expanding through the Sylvian fissure and basal cisterns without visible scolices.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Identifies ventricular outflow obstruction on emergency CT/MRI with acute triventricular dilation resulting from a mobile fourth ventricular or aqueductal cysticercal lesion.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Visualizes fourth ventricle dilation on brain CT/MRI caused by occlusion of the foramina of Luschka and Magendie by an intraventricular cysticercus or inflammatory ependymitis.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates secondary aqueductal stenosis on MRI caused by chronic ependymal inflammation and subependymal gliosis surrounding an aqueductal or fourth ventricular cyst.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals periventricular transependymal edema (capping) on T2/FLAIR MRI, indicating acute decompensated obstructive hydrocephalus requiring urgent neurosurgical CSF diversion.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Serves as the primary triage imaging modality on admission, possessing superior sensitivity over MRI for detecting punctate hyperdense calcified granulomas and acute ventriculomegaly.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Provides the definitive imaging modality for characterizing vesicular scolex detail, colloidal capsule enhancement, intraventricular lesions, and leptomeningeal inflammation.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Exhibits DWI non-restriction (dark on DWI, bright on ADC) within clear viable cysticercal fluid, providing a critical imaging differentiator against purulent bacterial brain abscesses.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Shows mildly elevated choline-to-creatine ratios and reduced NAA on proton MR spectroscopy within degenerating capsules, while lacking the massive malignant choline peaks of high-grade gliomas.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates a parasitic lactate and succinate peak on proton MR spectroscopy at 1.3 ppm reflecting cestode anaerobic carbohydrate metabolism within viable and colloidal cyst fluid.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Displays segmental arterial narrowing, irregular caliber beading, and occlusion of the middle or anterior cerebral arteries on angiography in basilar cisternal disease.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates continuous or intermittent focal polymorphic delta and theta wave slowing on EEG overlying cortical lobes containing active colloidal cysticerci.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Records focal spike-wave epileptiform discharges on interictal EEG conforming to cortical areas harboring calcified granulomas or colloidal lesions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates positive serum or CSF cysticercal antigen detection by monoclonal antibody ELISA (HP10 or B158), confirming viable cyst burden and monitoring response to anthelmintic therapy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Reveals Taenia species eggs or gravid proglottids on stool microscopy in only 10% to 15% of neurocysticercosis patients, confirming concurrent intestinal taeniasis.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals multiple elongated, 'cigar-shaped' calcifications aligned parallel to skeletal muscle fibers on plain X-rays of the thighs or arms, confirming disseminated cysticercosis.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals an anechoic intravitreal or subretinal cystic lesion with an eccentric hyperechoic mural nodule on ocular B-scan ultrasound, confirming intraocular cysticercosis.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates a small oval fluid-filled cavity with an eccentric hyperechoic nidus on bedside high-frequency POCUS of subcutaneous nodules, providing instant confirmatory evidence.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR < 20 mm/hr) on admission labs, contrasting sharply with the markedly elevated ESR seen in cerebral tuberculoma and bacterial abscess.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission triage lab, diagnostic pattern
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows normal serum C-reactive protein (<5-10 mg/L) at hospital triage, ruling out systemic bacterial infection and intracranial pyogenic collections.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Visualizes on contrast-enhanced spine MRI as an intradural extramedullary or intramedullary cystic lesion with an eccentric scolex displacing the spinal cord.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted exclusively via the fecal-oral ingestion of microscopic Taenia solium eggs shed in the feces of an infected human tapeworm carrier, NOT from eating pork.

[EXPOSURE_TO] Poses high transmission risk through household contact or cohabitation with a human intestinal tapeworm carrier who sheds millions of infectious eggs into the shared domestic environment.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Ingested through drinking untreated municipal or surface water supplies contaminated with human fecal runoff containing hardy, environmental-resistant Taenia solium eggs.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired via ingestion of unwashed raw agricultural vegetables and salads irrigated with sewage-polluted water or fertilized with untreated human night soil.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Perpetuated in communities practicing free-roaming domestic pig husbandry, where scavenging swine ingest human feces containing eggs, completing the intermediate host cycle.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Driven environmentally by the lack of closed sanitary latrines and open defecation in rural villages, which contaminates soil and water sources accessible to humans and pigs.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Sustained by unregulated home slaughter and informal meat sales of cyst-infected pork, maintaining the reservoir of human intestinal tapeworm carriers.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Highly prevalent across endemic rural agricultural communities in Latin America, South Asia, and sub-Saharan Africa, where up to 30% of acquired epilepsy is attributable to NCC.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Disproportionately affects subsistence pig farmers and their household members due to continuous close proximity to infected swine and contaminated agricultural soil.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] High-risk exposure occurs when household cooks or food handlers harbor asymptomatic intestinal tapeworms and shed eggs onto shared food through poor hand hygiene.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Affects rural agricultural workers who work bare-handed in fields fertilized with human waste and lack clean water for hand hygiene during meals.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Endangers international travelers and emigrants from non-endemic countries who visit hyperendemic regions and consume contaminated food or water prepared by tapeworm carriers.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] The primary epidemiological reservoir is the household taeniasis carrier, who shed thousands of microscopic eggs daily and poses an extreme contagion risk to family members.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Frequently clusters in domestic close-contact networks and families, where secondary infection rates are dramatically elevated around an identifiable tapeworm carrier.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Characterized by prolonged clinical latency lasting 2 to 5 years (and up to 20 to 30 years) between initial egg ingestion and the appearance of the first neurological symptom.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Features a multi-year incubation period during which viable cysticerci maintain active immune tolerance and suppress local inflammation until spontaneous involution occurs.

[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Exhibits a highly variable incubation interval ranging from months in acute massive infections to decades in solitary parenchymal lesions that remain quiescent until calcification.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired via fecal-oral autoinfection in individuals harboring adult tapeworms through poor personal hand hygiene or reverse proglottid peristalsis into the stomach.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Endemic throughout rural agricultural regions of Latin America including Mexico, Guatemala, Peru, Ecuador, and Bolivia, where pig-raising and open defecation persist.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Highly endemic across South Asia, particularly in rural India and Nepal, where neurocysticercosis causes over one-third of all acquired adult-onset seizure disorders.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Widely endemic in sub-Saharan Africa including Uganda, Tanzania, Mozambique, and South Africa, driven by the expansion of smallholder pig farming without sanitation.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Prevalent in focal agrarian communities of Southeast Asia, including rural Vietnam, Laos, and Bali, where traditional swine husbandry and culinary habits favor transmission.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Ingestion of undercooked pork containing cysticerci ALONE without fecal egg contamination rules out neurocysticercosis; it produces adult intestinal taeniasis, NOT cysticercosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of turbid or purulent CSF with thousands of polymorphonuclear neutrophils rules out uncomplicated neurocysticercosis, indicating acute pyogenic bacterial meningitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Acute high spiking fevers (>39°C) with toxic delirium and rigors rule out typical parenchymal neurocysticercosis, which is an afebrile or low-grade inflammatory disorder.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Marked peripheral leukocytosis (>15,000 cells/uL) with prominent neutrophilic bandemia rules out uncomplicated parenchymal neurocysticercosis, pointing to acute bacterial sepsis or abscess.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Markedly restricted diffusion (bright on DWI with corresponding dark hypointense ADC map) within a ring-enhancing lesion rules out neurocysticercosis, confirming a pyogenic bacterial brain abscess.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of giant multilocular cystic lesions packed with internal daughter cysts rules out neurocysticercosis, confirming cerebral hydatid disease (echinococcosis).
[RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of floating, collapsed internal parasite membranes ('water-lily sign') within a large intracranial cyst rules out neurocysticercosis, establishing ruptured Echinococcus.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Thick, shaggy, grossly irregular enhancing margins with central necrosis and infiltrating neovascular parenchymal invasion rule out benign discrete neurocysticercosis cysts in favor of high-grade glioma.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid massive midline shift (>10-15 mm) with subfalcine herniation in the absence of severe hydrocephalus rules out solitary parenchymal cysticerci, indicating high-grade neoplasm or large hematoma.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Direct bony calvarial osteolysis and transdural scalp invasion rule out neurocysticercosis, establishing primary bone malignancy, metastatic carcinoma, or aggressive osteomyelitis.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of cystic lesions, mural nodules, ring enhancement, focal edema, or calcified granulomas on high-resolution contrast brain MRI/CT rules out active or inactive symptomatic neurocysticercosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Profound CSF hypoglycorrhachia (<20 mg/dL or CSF:serum ratio <0.2) rules out typical neurocysticercosis, strongly indicating acute bacterial or advanced tuberculous meningitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli on CSF Ziehl-Neelsen smear or positive GeneXpert MTB/RIF rules out neurocysticercosis, confirming tuberculous meningitis or intracranial tuberculoma.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Positive cryptococcal capsular antigen lateral flow assay in serum or CSF rules out neurocysticercosis, establishing cryptococcal meningoencephalitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Direct visualization of bacterial diplococci, bacilli, or cocci on CSF Gram stain rules out neurocysticercosis, diagnosing acute bacterial meningitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of a vividly enhancing, cauliflower-like fronded intraventricular vascular mass rules out cysticercosis, establishing choroid plexus papilloma.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Widespread diffuse cerebral microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted MRI rule out neurocysticercosis, indicating cerebral amyloid angiopathy or severe diffuse axonal injury.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Hyperacute, maximal-at-onset focal hemiplegia without seizures or headache in an elderly patient with severe atherothrombotic risk factors rules out neurocysticercosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Diffuse nodular 'sugar-coating' leptomeningeal enhancement with malignant cells on CSF cytology rules out benign neurocysticercosis, establishing leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Exposure strictly limited to undercooked beef rules out neurocysticercosis, because Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm) does not cause human cysticercosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Serum procalcitonin elevation >2.0 ng/mL at triage rules out uncomplicated neurocysticercosis, confirming invasive pyogenic bacterial infection or septic shock.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Severe chemosis, proptosis, periorbital edema, and bilateral painful ophthalmoplegia with cavernous filling defects rule out neurocysticercosis, diagnosing cavernous sinus thrombosis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cerebral tuberculoma: Tuberculomas display thick irregular nodular rim enhancement with central T2-hypointensity, systemic constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), positive chest X-ray, and negative EITB, whereas NCC has thin regular walls, eccentric scolex dot, afebrile presentation, and positive EITB.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Pyogenic brain abscess: Brain abscess presents with toxic fever, marked leukocytosis, elevated ESR/CRP, and hallmark central restricted diffusion (bright on DWI, dark on ADC), whereas NCC cysts show non-restricting fluid, afebrile course, and normal inflammatory labs.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cerebral echinococcosis: Echinococcus granulosus produces massive expansive unilocular cysts with internal daughter vesicles and floating membranes ('water lily' sign) devoid of an invaginated scolex dot, whereas NCC cysts are smaller (5-20 mm) and contain a distinct mural scolex.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from High-grade glioma: Glioblastoma exhibits thick shaggy irregular enhancing rims, central necrosis, rapid progressive clinical deterioration, infiltrative neovascularization, and elevated MRS choline-to-creatine ratio, unlike the discrete, self-limited, stage-specific morphology of NCC.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Brain metastases: Metastatic lesions typically appear at gray-white junctions with disproportionate extensive surrounding edema, solid nodular enhancement, known primary malignancy, and lack an eccentric scolex dot.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cerebral toxoplasmosis: Toxoplasmosis predominantly affects advanced HIV/AIDS patients (CD4 <100/uL), presenting as multiple basal ganglia target-enhancing lesions ('eccentric target sign') that respond to pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine, contrasting with immunocompetent NCC epidemiology and EITB seropositivity.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Tuberculous meningitis: TB meningitis presents with thick gelatinous basilar exudate, severe hypoglycorrhachia (CSF glucose <20 mg/dL), elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA), and pulmonary lesions, whereas cysticercotic meningitis has mild/normal glucose, positive LL-GP EITB, and cystic lesions on MRI.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cryptococcal meningitis: Cryptococcus presents in immunosuppressed patients with positive India ink prep, positive cryptococcal capsular antigen, and gelatinous pseudocysts ('soap bubble' lesions) in basal ganglia, whereas NCC features definitive metacestode scolices and negative fungal markers.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Primary CNS lymphoma: CNS lymphoma presents as dense, homogenous periventricular or subependymal enhancing masses with restricted diffusion in immunocompromised patients, completely lacking the cystic fluid cavity and mural scolex of NCC.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Arachnoid cyst: Congenital arachnoid cysts are extra-axial, perfectly isointense to CSF on all MRI sequences, lack wall enhancement or surrounding edema, have no mural scolex, and remain static in size over years.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Epidermoid cyst: Epidermoid tumors grow along cisterns by creeping into crevices, show marked hyperintensity on DWI with restricted diffusion, and lack inflammatory capsule enhancement or scolex.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Neurovascular stroke: Atherothrombotic stroke presents acutely in older patients with vascular risk factors and territorial vascular wedge distribution, whereas NCC-related stroke occurs in young endemic patients with basilar cisternal cysts causing endarteritis obliterans.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Viral encephalitis: Herpes simplex encephalitis presents with acute fever, confusion, temporal lobe T2/FLAIR hyperintensity with hemorrhagic changes, and positive HSV PCR, unlike afebrile focal seizures caused by discrete NCC parenchymal cysts.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Intracranial hydatid cyst: Hydatid disease produces large spherical cysts that can grow up to 10 cm in diameter with calcified pericyst walls, unlike typical parenchymal cysticercosis cysts which measure only 5 to 20 mm.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Bacterial meningitis: Acute bacterial meningitis presents with fulminant fever, septic shock, cloudy CSF with thousands of neutrophils, low glucose, and positive Gram stain/culture, whereas cysticercotic meningitis is chronic, afebrile, and lymphocytic.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Multiple sclerosis: MS produces demyelinating periventricular Dawson fingers, open-ring enhancements, CSF oligoclonal bands, and relapsing-remitting deficits, lacking discrete round cysts with scolices.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Cavernous malformation: Cerebral cavernomas exhibit a characteristic 'popcorn' appearance with a complete hemosiderin hypointense rim on gradient echo/SWI sequences without scolex or true fluid-filled cyst cavity.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Colloid cyst: Third ventricle colloid cysts arise strictly at the foramen of Monro with hyperdense T1-shortening mucinous contents, whereas intraventricular NCC cysts are mobile, located commonly in the fourth ventricle, and contain an invaginated scolex.
